#### What this PR does / why we need it:

No scheduling info captured if the logging level less than 10. It would be a little help to find what happend if the top N highest node/plugin scores dumped at a lower level.

@damemi made some improvement in #99411 , however it is found ~50% performace drop in large cluster. 

As @Huang-Wei suggests in  #101820，we use a dynamical logging strategy to dump depending on the logging level:
- for logging level ranged in [4, 6), dump the scores for topM nodes/plugins. And make it as performant as possible.
- for logging level ranged in [6, 10), dump the scores for topN nodes, and probably show all plugins
- for logging level >= 10, dump the scores for all nodes/plugins.

issue_context.title: More debug logs to check scheduler spread algorithm
issue_context.body:
/sig scheduling 

#### What would you like to be added:
A way to check the scoring of each node to figure out why a node has a high scheduling priority.

- proposal 1: add **some debug level logs** to Kube-scheduler, so we can know node score on each scoring step.
- proposal 2: a simple way to decrease the priority of one node(in my case a node with more than 200 pods is with the highest scheduling priority for an unknown reason) 
- proposal 3:?

All new pods are scheduled to one of five nodes in my cluster.
I have checked both CPU/memory requested usage and all five nodes are bare metal and running about 150 pods or 200 pods.
Pods on node request 80-93% of the memory. 

#### Why is this needed:

We have a similar issue as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/73843.

Currently, I think `proposal 1` is the easiest way.
comments:
This is useful. how do you suggest we log this information? note that there are two dimensions for each pod: plugin and node score.

Also, we need to limit the log length, we can't simply log the score for each node in clusters with large number of nodes.

> Also, we need to limit the log length, we can't simply log the score for each node in clusters with large number of nodes.

@ahg-g I prefer to log only the top 5 or 10 node scores in the log. (I have not read the code yet.😄, will dig into it later.)

We actually merged something like this that I wrote in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/99411, but had to revert it because of performance issue in large clusters. That could be a good starting point @pacoxu 

My general approach was to 1) invert the `scoresMap` already available to map `node->plugins` (rather than `plugin->nodeScores`, which it currently does) and then 2) log the top 3 highest scoring plugins for each node

However @Huang-Wei discovered performance issues after this in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99913 (we believe due to the many writes this process took) and it was reverted in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/99914. I think we decided that *some* performance hit is reasonable, especially given log levels >=4, but this was ~50% drop.
@pacoxu yes, that's the current case. Though `V(10)` creates a *lot* of other noise in the logs, so I think we agreed that it is okay for us to add this kind of summary at a lower level like `V(4)`

I think we can use this chance to standardize the logging logic to dump scores dynamically depending on log level:

- for logging level ranged in `[4, 6)`, dump the scores for topM nodes/plugins. And make it as performant as possible.
- for logging level ranged in `[6, 10)`, dump the scores for topN nodes, and probably show all plugins
- for logging level >= 10, dump the scores for all nodes/plugins.
/assign
/triage accepted
